sourceLabel: Video statement posted to X.

[...] I’ve been hearing about the existential threat to humankind for years. And I’ll be honest, I’m not sure everyone in Congress has been doing the same. [...] We’ve seen harbingers of the threats that this technology holds as researchers and developers lose control of rogue collusive AI agents, and the technology is advancing far more rapidly than we originally assumed it would. It’s science fiction come to life.
sourceLabel: Thread on X.
notes: Sourced via AIPN Congress on Superintelligence

[...] Here’s the challenge. We have to put some guardrails, some safety measures in place to ensure that AI doesn’t run away, you know, that we don’t have an out-of-control AGI, artificial general intelligence. But at the same time, we’ve got to make sure that we don’t lose our edge in the global competition on this with China. Because that would be a national security threat.
sourceLabel: Speaker of the House, on NBC's Meet the Press.
notes: Sourced via AIPN Congress on Superintelligence

quote: [Quote-tweeting David Sacks, co-chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology: "Dario has written that we need to “pace the frontier,” and Sam has agreed. AI isn’t going anywhere, so we need a plan to move forward safely, with America leading the way. These companies have said what they are building could kill mankind. If America doesn’t lead, we allow Communist China to make the rules and develop truly dangerous AI that will hurt Americans, especially our kids. Congress is a mess right now. AI companies need to be good corporate citizens, protect our kids' safety online and do the right thing without fear of their bottom line.

notes: Sourced via AIPN Congress on Superintelligence

notes: Sourced via AIPN Congress on Superintelligence

And that includes implementing mandatory safeguards and a comprehensive testing regime. [...] This should not be a partisan issue. The impact of AI on our collective future, on our safety, on our security, on our economy and on our shared humanity must be the type of risk that brings us all together. [...] I don’t know about my Republican colleagues, but I think that’s a big deal. [...] We’re talking about a greater than 10 percent chance we could all be dead soon if we don’t do something to radically change the way we regulate and oversee AI. [...] Either way, we clearly need to act.

notes: Sourced via AIPN Congress on Superintelligence

And this deep concern about the rapidly emerging artificial superintelligence is certainly well founded. [...] [Networks of agents] are extremely well informed. They operate at the speed of light and, as we are learning, they are also capable of creating their own goals, and they are highly capable of deception. [...] The technology keeps advancing. The risks keep growing and now the very dangers we've warned about — autonomous cyberattacks and biological weapons — are no longer theoretical.

notes: Sourced via AIPN Congress on Superintelligence

And it doesn’t share our values. It doesn’t share human values. Now, that has happened. We’ve read about it in the last three weeks. [...] In my mind, if there is even a 1% chance that one of these AI models can shed its nature as a tool and become an independent species and start doing whatever the hell it wants to do, if there’s even a 1% chance, we ought to take it seriously.

notes: Sourced via AIPN Congress on Superintelligence
